demo_steps.narration: The default view matches the textbook: staggered on the left with evenly alternating hydrogens, eclipsed on the right with overlapping pairs and three 4.0 kJ/mol braces. The arrow indicates the 60° rotation connecting them.

demo_steps.title: Rotate back to staggered

Front H azimuths fixed at 90°, 210°, 330°. Rear H group offset: at slider=0 rear Hs are at 30°, 150°, 270° (staggered); at slider=60 rear Hs are at 90°, 210°, 330° (eclipsed). Newman projection H labels: front in green #2faa44, rear in magenta #cc22aa. Curly braces at radius 1.3 from Newman center, opacity = clamp((slider-20)/40), color #222222. Arrow: horizontal line from x=-1.2 to x=+1.2 at y=0 with arrowhead, label 'Rotate rear carbon 60°' above it in black. Panel labels below each ball-and-stick model in bold black. Ball-and-stick models oriented with C-C axis along local Z tilted ~15° toward camera to give slight oblique view showing 3D depth. Staggered caption only visible on left panel; eclipsed caption only on right panel — they are separate text objects at different x positions so no overlap is possible.
plan.notes: Build as two independent panel groups (leftGroup, rightGroup) each containing a Newman sub-group and a ball-and-stick sub-group. The left panel is completely static. The right panel's rearGroup rotates about its local Z axis by -(60 - sliderValue) degrees so slider=60 gives eclipsed and slider=0 gives staggered. Newman projection rear bond angles update identically. Curly braces and energy labels are children of the right Newman group with opacity driven by the slider. Use raycasting on the three brace meshes and the six right-panel H spheres for click highlighting. Orbit controls rotate the entire scene; Newman projections should be billboarded (always face camera) using a per-frame lookAt or onBeforeRender callback. Keep captions as separate sprite/text objects at distinct world positions (left at x=-3 y=-2.2, right at x=+3 y=-2.2) to prevent any overlap.

authoredPrompt: This figure compares two conformations of ethane, each shown as a Newman projection paired with a ball-and-stick model, with a reaction-style arrow between them. On the left, the Newman projection draws the front carbon as a dot at the center of a circle with three heavy bonds radiating up, down-left, and down-right to hydrogens lettered in green, while the rear carbon is the circle itself with three thinner bonds emerging at the left, right, and bottom to hydrogens lettered in magenta, so the two sets alternate evenly. Its ball-and-stick model, viewed end-on, shows a dark gray carbon ringed by three green and three red spheres in alternating positions. The horizontal arrow between the halves is labeled "Rotate rear carbon 60°". On the right, the projection shows each front bond lying directly over a rear bond, so the green and magenta hydrogens appear in overlapping pairs, and three curly braces, one at each pair, are each labeled "4.0 kJ/mol". The matching model now shows the green and red spheres in coincident pairs. Bold labels read "Ethane—staggered conformation" and "Ethane—eclipsed conformation". Setting the two projections side by side makes the hydrogen spacing the thing being compared, and the three equal energy labels partition the rotational barrier into individual eclipsing interactions.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the rear carbon from 0 to 60 degrees; the Newman projection and ball-and-stick model update continuously from staggered to eclipsed, making torsional alignment the source of the conformational change.
- Click for highlighting one eclipsed H-H pair; its brace and 4.0 kJ/mol label brighten along with the overlapping hydrogens, clarifying how three identical interactions add to the rotational barrier.
authoredContext:
Despite what we’ve just said, we actually don’t observe perfectly free rotation in ethane. Experiments show that there is a small (12 kJ/mol; 2.9 kcal/mol) barrier to rotation and that some conformations are more stable than others. The lowest-energy, most stable conformation is the one in which all six C–H bonds are as far away from one another as possible—staggered when viewed end-on in a Newman projection. The highest-energy, least stable conformation is the one in which the six C–H bonds are as close as possible—eclipsed in a Newman projection. At any given instant, about 99% of ethane molecules have an approximately staggered conformation and only about 1% are near the eclipsed conformation.

Staggered conformation of ethane undergoes rotation of rear carbon 60 degrees to form eclipsed conformation of ethane.

The extra 12 kJ/mol of energy present in the eclipsed conformation of ethane is called torsional strain. Its cause has been the subject of controversy, but the major factor is an interaction between C–H bonding orbitals on one carbon and antibonding orbitals on the adjacent carbon, which stabilizes the staggered conformation relative to the eclipsed one. Because a total strain of 12 kJ/mol arises from three equal hydrogen–hydrogen eclipsing interactions, we can assign a value of approximately 4.0 kJ/mol (1.0 kcal/mol) to each single interaction. The barrier to rotation that results can be represented on a graph of potential energy versus degree of rotation, in which the angle between C–H bonds on the front and back carbons as viewed end-on (the dihedral angle) goes full circle from 0 to 360°. Energy minima occur at staggered conformations, and energy maxima occur at eclipsed conformations, as shown in the figure.
sourceQmd: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 3: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry

demo_steps.title: Staggered (0°)
demo_steps.narration: At 0° the rear hydrogens sit exactly between the front hydrogens (60° dihedral). The Newman projection shows the two sets alternating evenly and the ball-and-stick model shows green and red spheres interleaved — minimum torsional strain.

demo_steps.title: Mid-rotation (30°)
demo_steps.narration: Halfway through the rotation each rear H is drifting toward a front H; the braces begin to fade in as the pairs start to overlap, showing the barrier building continuously.

demo_steps.title: Eclipsed (60°)
demo_steps.narration: At 60° every rear bond lies directly behind a front bond. Three curly braces each read 4.0 kJ/mol — click any pair to isolate one of the three equal eclipsing interactions that sum to the ~12 kJ/mol barrier.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale in Ångström-like units: C-C bond 1.5 along the depth (Z) axis, front C at z=+0.75, rear C at z=-0.75; C-H bonds 1.1 long, perpendicular to the C-C axis. Carbon spheres radius 0.35 color #3a3a3a; front H spheres radius 0.22 green #2faa44; rear H spheres radius 0.22 red #cc3333; bond cylinders radius 0.06 color #c0c0c0. Front H azimuths fixed at 90°, 210°, 330° (up, lower-left, lower-right); rear H group built at front+60° and rotated about Z by -slider so slider=60 gives 0° offset (eclipsed). Newman overlay is a camera-facing flat group placed to the left (world x≈-3, z≈+2): outer circle radius 0.8 (rear C), center dot radius 0.07 (front C), thick front lines length 0.95 to green 'H' glyphs, thin rear lines length 0.5 from rim to magenta 'H' glyphs rotating with the same angle. Three curly braces at radius ~1.25 from the Newman center aligned to the three pair directions, each with a '4.0 kJ/mol' label; brace/label opacity = clamp((slider-30)/30) and the clicked pair is boosted to full brightness with its two H spheres emissive-highlighted. Caption text swaps at slider=30. Palette: green #2faa44, magenta #cc22aa, red #cc3333, carbon #3a3a3a, bonds #c0c0c0, labels/braces #222222.
interactionPlan.notes: Build two THREE.Group sub-trees: frontGroup (fixed) and rearGroup (rotated about the bond axis by -dihedral). The Newman overlay is a separate orthographic-feeling group of Line/LineLoop + sprite/text meshes parented to the camera or kept in a fixed screen plane so it stays front-on even when orbitView rotates the molecule. Recompute rear-group quaternion and brace opacities on every slider input; use raycasting against the six H spheres (or the three brace meshes) for the click highlight, storing a highlightedPair index in {-1,0,1,2}. Keep both staggered and eclipsed captions in the scene and toggle visibility rather than rebuilding text. Render H-H pair braces as quadratic-Bezier tube/line curls; fade them with material.opacity tied to the dihedral so the energy annotation emerges exactly as eclipsing occurs.
